title: THE 2026 INDUSTRY PULSE REPORT — U.K. Edition

study_design.objective: Survey U.K. buy- and sell-side digital media experts on 2026 challenges and opportunities
study_design.participants: N=220 U.K. digital media experts who use programmatic advertising (Advertisers n=84; Agencies n=81; Publishers & platforms n=55)

key_insights: Media experts are prioritising digital video (87%) and digital display (81%) as top digital formats, while digital audio lags (55%)
Social media remains the top priority digital environment among media experts
The industry must balance innovation with control as generative AI, MFA sites, and adjacency risks threaten media quality
Media experts generally feel positively about advertising near generative AI content, with success hinging on quality controls aligned to brand values
Gen AI content with inaccuracies, cluttered UX, bot traffic, plagiarism/regurgitation, or unverifiable domains is widely deemed unsuitable for adjacency
Social media faces the most serious challenges (41%), followed by digital video (31%), digital display (29%), and influencer marketing (27%)
In CTV, attention (84%), brand safety (82%), and ad fraud (76%) are growing concerns as inventory volume and sellers increase

In retail media networks, attention (84%), viewability (82%), and brand suitability (82%) are important to performance; influencer suitability (78%) and AI content levels (77%) are key adjacency considerations

sections.title: Top Media Challenges and Opportunities
sections.summary: As digital media evolves, opportunities on social media and digital video come with complexity. The rise of generative AI, MFA sites, and adjacency risks threaten media quality; the challenge is balancing innovation with control to drive trust and performance

sections.title: The Rise of Generative AI
sections.summary: Generative AI has shifted from experimentation to an essential tool, bringing speed, personalisation, and scale alongside new risks. Media experts are generally positive about advertising near AI-generated content when paired with quality controls. Not all AI content is equal; marketers should avoid inaccurate, cluttered, bot-attracting, plagiarised, or unverifiable domains

sections.title: Social Media
sections.summary: Social media fuels cultural conversations and shapes decisions; advertisers seek brand-safe spaces that foster trust and relevancy

sections.title: Digital Video
sections.summary: Digital video continues explosive growth across mobile and social feeds. Viewability and brand safety of placements remain critical to transparency and impact

sections.title: Connected TV
sections.summary: CTV blends linear impact with digital precision; as ad-supported models proliferate, marketers demand clearer insights into performance, reach, and quality. Media quality concerns around attention, brand safety, and fraud will be prevalent

sections.title: Retail Media Networks
sections.summary: Retail media has evolved into a powerhouse of digital commerce with unmatched precision, introducing challenges around measurement and quality assurance. Media quality is foundational to success; attention, viewability, and suitability matter, and influencer suitability and AI content levels are key adjacency considerations
